method.scope: Only the plugin surface was read: src/core.ts and src/platform.ts, plus the modules those two files import (e.g. coveru/src/zip-file-reader.ts, classf/src/blacklist.ts, findz/src/worker-client.ts). src/cli.ts, src/Tui.tsx, src/help.ts and src/interaction.ts are excluded by design.
method.authoritativeCapability: Each node's `*Runtime` interface in core.ts is treated as the capability contract, because it is the only object core.ts can call. A platform.ts helper that is not a runtime member is host-side dead weight for the plugin surface.
method.keyDiscovery: 23 of 41 retained nodes define the same `readClipboardText()` block in platform.ts (powershell.exe Get-Clipboard / pbpaste / wl-paste / xclip / xsel). Exactly 1 of those reaches it from core.ts — classf, whose runtime member readClipboardPaths (classf/src/core.ts:53) is called at classf/src/core.ts:87. The other 22 are reached only from cli.ts (e.g. crashu/src/cli.ts:31,440), so for 22 of 41 nodes clipboard is NOT a node-core capability. `cliOnlySpawn` in each record holds those binaries so they are never counted as node demand.
method.fileIoPrecedence: fileIo is the most demanding class the node performs, chosen from positionalRead > recursiveEnumeration > contentReadWrite > singleDirList > none; fileIoAll records every class that applies.
method.spawnConvention: spawn lists only programs reachable from a runtime member. `where.exe`/`which` are recorded as locators, not payload commands. Binaries reached only through the cli-side clipboard block are listed under cliOnlySpawn instead.
method.crateVerification: Every crate in existingCrates was fetched from the crates.io API on 2026-10-05 and is reported as name@max_stable_version with its last-updated date. `stale` marks a crate whose date or release count makes it a weak pick; `unverified` marks a capability with no crate I could confirm.

drift: No node-list drift: all 41 `retain-rewrite` ids have a directory under packages/nodes/, and the 6 `removed` ids (arcthumb, czkawka, gitalso, scoalp, vert, xlchemy) plus the 1 `drop-to-standalone` id (neoview) have none. No directory exists that the manifest does not name.
xiranite.build.toml `[nodes].disabled` = ["clipm", "kisaki", "lata"] matches the 3 `hold-unmigrated` entries exactly. The three legs of `bun run audit:target-node-manifest` agree.
Minor: packages/nodes/.DS_Store is a stray directory entry that is not a node; the audit gate evidently tolerates it.

AGENTS.md CLAIM NOT BACKED BY CODE: 'trename 的中译英词典是 SQLite/FTS 文件' — zero matches for sqlite/FTS/dictionary/opencc/translation anywhere under packages/nodes/trename (core.ts, platform.ts and the rest of src/). trename today has no dictionary of any kind, so ADR-0071's SQLite-in-plugin spike question is moot for the current node; the dictionary is a not-yet-built feature, not a present dependency.

AGENTS.md CLAIM CONFIRMED: 'smartzip 读 ZIP 尾 32 MiB' is real and already positional in TypeScript today (smartzip/src/platform.ts:270-273 reads an 8-byte signature at offset 0, then a tail of up to 32 MiB at info.size - tailSize). NOT IN AGENTS.md: lorat is a third positional reader. Its fileId hash reads the first 1 MiB at offset 0 and the last 1 MiB at info.size - chunkSize (lorat/src/platform.ts:149-159). It belongs in the same list as smartzip and coveru.

blockers: The only retained node that is not a port of pure logic. Its entire business implementation is a Go library (native/findz-go, CGo mattn/go-sqlite3, ffi.go) loaded through FFI and driven from a persistent Bun worker with @parcel/watcher; core.ts is a JSON-RPC client for it (findz/src/core.ts:14 worker-client.js).

Making it a plain native Rust crate means re-implementing the scanner, the SQLite index, the archive member model, the image analysis, the pause/resume/cancel task state machine AND the watcher — i.e. a rewrite, not a port. The manifest already records wasmFeasibility blocked-native; that verdict still holds in the native world for a different reason.
Persistent state: it owns a per-library .sqlite file (database.go:306) that survives runs, unlike every other retained node.
